clues: A vast capital spreads over a dry northern plain, ringed by mountains on three sides, near the old corridor that leads west to the steppe.
Winters are bitter, bone-dry, and dust-blown off the deserts; summers turn hot and wet when the monsoon finally pushes this far north.
Steppe khans built their capital here in the 1200s; later emperors raised a walled palace city at its heart that stood for five centuries.
Its main square is the largest public square on earth, and a wall twenty-one thousand kilometers long snakes over the mountains just north of town.
The Forbidden City's golden roofs still fill the old center, ringed by its great red walls.
